newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN rights chief to visit Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UN rights chief to visit Rwanda.

text.p: U.N. human rights chief Jose Ayala Lasso will go to Rwanda soon to find out more about the killing of five of his staff last week, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Therese Gastaut said the rights chief will seek the result of a government investigation into the killings when he visits the tiny central African country late this week or next week.

Ayala Lasso, criticised by some diplomats and human rights groups for his relatively low profile in drawing public attention to abuses and violence, was also expected to re-examine the security situation in Rwanda.

His staff have criticised Ayala Lasso for not going to Rwanda immediately after the killings of four U.N. human rights monitors -- a Briton, a Cambodian and two Rwandans -- in an ambush last Tuesday in Cyangugu in southwestern Rwanda. Their Rwandan driver later died of his wounds.

The Briton, 36-year-old Graham Turnbull, was buried near his home in York at the weekend. Turnbull was teamleader for human rights observers in Cyangugu. He had only recently warned his colleagues about the growing dangers in the region, where Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army is fighting majority Hutu rebels.
A wave of recent attacks on aid workers in Rwanda have underlined the vulnerability of relief staff in conflict zones.
